overview.title: Student & Teacher Overview: Lesson 1
overview.pill: Module 2 • Addition and Subtraction of Integers and Rational Numbers
overview.text: In this lesson on Opposite Quantities Combine to Make Zero, explore proportional reasoning, rational number operations, algebraic equations, or geometric proofs aligned with national Common Core standards.
outcomes: Develop conceptual understanding and fluency with Opposite Quantities Combine to Make Zero.
Apply properties of operations and proportional reasoning to formulate models and equations.
Demonstrate precision in problem solving and communicate mathematical reasoning using clear mathematical notation.
overview.teacherInsight: Emphasize the transition from visual tape diagrams and double number lines to formal algebraic equations ($y = kx$, $p + q$, $I = Prt$). Guide students to verify their solutions by substituting values back into original expressions.

vocabulary.definition: The constant value of the ratio between two proportional quantities, typically denoted by $k = \frac{y}{x}$.
Any number that can be expressed as the quotient or fraction $\frac{p}{q}$ of two integers, with the denominator $q \ne 0$.
The number that, when added to a given number, yields zero ($a + (-a) = 0$).

problemSet.title: Official Worksheet: Problem Set & Practice
problemSet.description: Work through these curriculum problem set exercises for Opposite Quantities Combine to Make Zero. Record your steps in the digital workspace and check with the teacher solutions.

problems.title: Problem 1: Signed Number Operations
problems.prompt: Evaluate the expression: $-14 - (-26) + (-18) \times (-2)$. Show each step using the rules of additive inverses and signed multiplication.
problems.problem: Evaluate the expression: $-14 - (-26) + (-18) \times (-2)$. Show each step using the rules of additive inverses and signed multiplication.
problems.hint: Multiply negative numbers first: $(-18) \times (-2) = +36$. Then rewrite subtraction as adding the opposite.

problems.title: Problem 2: Distance on a Number Line
problems.prompt: A scuba diver descends to a depth of $-38.5\text{ meters}$. A nearby research station sits at an elevation of $12.4\text{ meters}$ above sea level. Determine the vertical distance between the station and the diver.
problems.problem: A scuba diver descends to a depth of $-38.5\text{ meters}$. A nearby research station sits at an elevation of $12.4\text{ meters}$ above sea level. Determine the vertical distance between the station and the diver.
problems.hint: Distance between $p$ and $q$ on a number line is given by the absolute difference $|p - q|$.

problems.title: Problem 3: Rational Fraction to Decimal Conversion
problems.prompt: Convert $-\frac{7}{12}$ to a decimal using long division. State whether the decimal terminates or repeats, and represent any repeating block with bar notation.
problems.problem: Convert $-\frac{7}{12}$ to a decimal using long division. State whether the decimal terminates or repeats, and represent any repeating block with bar notation.
problems.hint: Divide $7$ by $12$. Observe the remainder after the tenths digit.
problems.solution: $7 \div 12 = 0.58333\dots$. Therefore, $-\frac{7}{12} = -0.58\bar{3}$. It is an eventually repeating non-terminating decimal.

steps.action: Apply negative sign and bar notation
